title: The Khalsa Reads the Invasion as a Divinely Timed Opening

blocks.text: This page explains how the Khalsa interpreted the Persian invasion. Since Mughal power was already devouring itself, the Singhs say that one thorn removes a thorn: one violent force can uproot another and expose the weakness of Delhi’s persecuting regime.

Prophetic language then frames the crisis as long foreseen. A hound from Kabul is said to have descended upon Hindustan, and the page links that prophecy to the chance for the Khalsa to regroup, shout Akal, and step forward without waiting for favor from any court.

Kapoor Singh emerges as the leader who recognizes the moment clearly. He urges the Panth to treat the invasion not as chaos alone but as an opening in which the persecuted community can recover initiative and act with confidence.
